slides.title:
The name is not
a design choice.
slides.body:
Euljiro is full of cafes styled to look old. This one works from the other direction. 'Hanyakbang' means herbal medicine shop, and the name points at what this pocket of central Seoul used to be — the area is tied to Hyeminseo, the Joseon dynasty's public medical office, which the Korea Herald connects to the royal physician Heo Jun.

So the slowness is the point. Coffee is roasted by hand and poured by hand, closer to steeping medicine than pulling a shot, and the room around it is furnished with objects that were actually collected rather than ordered to match.

Getting in is part of it. The entrance is off a narrow alley between Euljiro's office towers, and there is no shopfront to aim for.

caption:
A Seoul coffeehouse you will probably walk past twice before you find the door.

Coffee Hanyakbang, Euljiro: down a narrow alley off Samil-daero 12-gil, named after a herbal medicine shop, with hand-poured filter coffee and a room full of collected antiques.

Hours differ by day, so check before you go.
